method.method_draft: First describe the image and locate each label along the titration progression. Then map the labels to chemical stages: A is initial weak acid only, B is partial neutralization where HA and A− coexist, C is near equivalence, D is equivalence/steep-change region, and E is excess strong base. Because a buffer is the HA/A− mixture formed during partial neutralization, choose point B.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The image is a titration curve with pH on the vertical axis and Base Added on the horizontal axis. The curve starts at low pH at point A on the left, rises gently to a relatively flat region containing point B, then begins to rise more noticeably around point C. It then enters a steep vertical rise around point D and finally levels off at high pH near point E.

Reasoning: In a weak monoprotic acid titrated with a strong base, A corresponds to the initial weak acid solution before much base has been added. B lies in the partial-neutralization region, where both the weak acid HA and its conjugate base A− are present. C is near the approach to equivalence, D is in the equivalence/steep-change region, and E represents excess strong base after equivalence. A buffered solution occurs when appreciable amounts of HA and A− coexist, so the buffered point is B.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the curve positions of A–E. planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to identify the titration as weak monoprotic acid plus strong base, which determines the relevant conjugate acid-base pair and the order of titration stages.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: During titration of a weak monoprotic acid HA with strong base, added OH− converts some HA to A−. Before equivalence, especially around the middle of the pre-equivalence region, both HA and A− coexist, forming a buffer. At the initial point there is mostly HA; at equivalence there is mostly A−; after equivalence there is excess OH−.
